A regular hexagon can be divided into six equilateral triangles by drawing lines from the center to each vertex. The sides of these triangles are equal to the side length of the hexagon. 

The perimeter of one equilateral triangle is given as 21 inches. Since an equilateral triangle has three equal sides, each side is \( 21 \div 3 = 7 \) inches. 

This side length is also the side length of the regular hexagon. A regular hexagon has 6 sides, so its perimeter is \( 6 \times 7 = 42 \) inches.

Answer: 42

Let the side length of the equilateral triangle be s. Then its perimeter is 3s = 21 inches => s = 7 inches.

In a regular hexagon divided into 6 equilateral triangles from the center, the side length of each equilateral triangle is equal to the side length of the hexagon. So the hexagon has side length s = 7 inches. A regular hexagon has 6 sides, so its perimeter is 6 * 7 = 42 inches.

Thus the perimeter of the hexagon is 42 inches.
